allowedInputs: same requestId and same mutation durable replay
same requestId and different mutation conflict
NEW.diskState: No transaction row exists for a genuinely new requestId; durable terminal history may exist for replay.
NEW.vaultState: Must equal the current authority-event-chain head projection.
NEW.metadataState: Must equal the current authority-event-chain head projection.
NEW.runtimeState: SQLite, AppRuntime and SecureBridge must share the last accepted FD5/FD6 boundary.
NEW.recovery: Replay a validated terminal result, reject a mutation conflict, or create PREPARING through the serialized coordinator.

PREPARING.diskState: A sealed transaction row exists with before/after images, digests, metadata boundaries and stateHistory ending in PREPARING.
PREPARING.runtimeState: Must remain at previousGeneration and must not expose the candidate mutation.
PREPARING.recovery: Deterministically roll back to the prior authority boundary; invalid or unsealed history fails closed.

PREPARED.diskState: The sealed journal contains the complete candidate and stateHistory ending in PREPARED.
PREPARED.runtimeState: Must remain at previousGeneration; the candidate may exist only as non-authoritative in-memory staging.
PREPARED.recovery: QUERY with the same requestId; if PREPARED, continue the same transaction or ABORT. If QUERY is impossible, terminate the backend as indeterminate.

COMMITTING.diskState: The sealed journal records COMMITTING before vault replacement. Vault and metadata may each be at the before or after boundary only.
COMMITTING.vaultState: May equal beforeRaw or afterRaw; no third image is legal.
COMMITTING.metadataState: May equal previousMetadata or nextMetadata; no unrelated generation is legal.
COMMITTING.runtimeState: Must not advance until Electron returns a committed authority-event binding and all backend authorities accept it.
COMMITTING.recovery: Use before/after digests plus the authority chain to complete commit or rollback. Any unmatched combination fails closed.

allowedInputs: compensating ABORT after backend authority failure
COMMITTED.diskState: A sealed COMMITTED transaction and TRANSACTION_COMMITTED authority event exist and form the current or validated historical chain boundary.
COMMITTED.vaultState: For the current boundary, must equal afterRaw and the event vaultDigest/referenceCount.
COMMITTED.metadataState: For the current boundary, must equal nextMetadata and the authority-event-chain head.
COMMITTED.runtimeState: Either all SQLite/AppRuntime/SecureBridge authorities accepted the same committed boundary, or the backend must compensate and not remain RUNNING.
COMMITTED.recovery: Complete any missing vault/metadata projection from the durable authority event; a terminal mismatch with no legal explanation fails closed.

ABORTING.diskState: ABORTING is durably sealed before rollback side effects; the rollback authority event is durable before vault/metadata projection.
ABORTING.vaultState: May equal afterRaw or beforeRaw only while rollback is being completed.
ABORTING.metadataState: May equal nextMetadata or previousMetadata only while rollback is being completed.
ABORTING.runtimeState: Must be restored to the saved previous authority token before normal operation resumes.
ABORTING.recovery: Complete rollback from the durable rollback event. Journal failure before side effects leaves the prior committed authority intact and makes the live Host unavailable.

ROLLED_BACK.diskState: A sealed ROLLED_BACK transaction and rollback authority event exist as a validated historical/current boundary.
ROLLED_BACK.vaultState: For the current boundary, must equal beforeRaw and the rollback event digest/referenceCount.
ROLLED_BACK.metadataState: For the current boundary, must equal previousMetadata and the rollback authority boundary.
ROLLED_BACK.runtimeState: SQLite, AppRuntime and SecureBridge must remain or be restored to previousGeneration and prior references.
ROLLED_BACK.recovery: Return the durable non-persisted result without re-executing the mutation. Current-boundary mismatches fail closed.

FAILED.diskState: A sealed FAILED transaction records a definite failure that occurred before an authoritative mutation or after a completed safe rollback.
FAILED.vaultState: Must equal the authority boundary recorded for the failure.
FAILED.metadataState: Must equal the same authority boundary.
FAILED.runtimeState: Must not advance for the failed request; a definite pre-side-effect failure leaves the prior known runtime authority intact.
FAILED.recovery: Return the durable failure for replay. A healthy Host may accept a different request; if the failure also made authority durability uncertain, the Host is separately marked unavailable and startup/recovery must fail closed.

INDETERMINATE.diskState: No success/failure may be inferred from transport state; durable journal and authority-event-chain data remain the only recovery evidence.
INDETERMINATE.vaultState: Unknown to the backend until Electron QUERY/restart recovery validates it.
INDETERMINATE.metadataState: Unknown to the backend until Electron QUERY/restart recovery validates it.
INDETERMINATE.runtimeState: Generation is unknown; no new custody mutation may be accepted.
INDETERMINATE.recovery: QUERY by the same requestId. If QUERY cannot establish a terminal result, invoke onIndeterminateCommit exactly once, controlled-shutdown the backend, and rebuild authority through the next strict FD5 hydration.

globalRules: Every stateHistory transition must be legal under the shared state-machine module.
Only CredentialVaultHost may mutate vault bytes.
No backend can remain RUNNING while credential generation or outcome is unknown.
